## What this letter says

This letter gives the results of your camera test (gastroscopy). It also gives the results of your stomach biopsies. And it tells you the plan.

- The biopsies show no cancer.
- There is no sign of an infection called Helicobacter pylori.
- The biopsies did show some changes. They are called intestinal metaplasia.
- This is not cancer. It is a change in the lining of your stomach.
- In a small number of people, it can change more over many years.
- So the hospital will keep an eye on it.

## What you need to do

1. Keep taking omeprazole as before.
2. Do not take ibuprofen. Do not take other anti-inflammatory painkillers. The letter says they can irritate the stomach.
3. If you need a painkiller, you can take paracetamol instead.
4. You do not need to do anything now about your next camera test. The hospital will send you an appointment.

## Dates and medicines

Dates:
- 8 September 2026: you had the camera test (gastroscopy). Biopsies were taken.
- Around September 2029: your next camera test. This is in 3 years.

Medicines:
- Omeprazole, 20 milligrams, once a day. Keep taking it. No change.
- Ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers: stop taking them.
- Paracetamol: you can use this instead, if you need a painkiller.

## Questions to ask your doctor

- What is a biopsy?
- What does intestinal metaplasia mean for me?
- How will you keep an eye on the change in my stomach?
- Which painkillers are anti-inflammatory painkillers?

## When to get urgent help

The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
